newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Johnnic's "black share" allotment delayed.
newsitem.headline: Johnnic's "black share" allotment delayed.

text.p: South Africa's Johnnies Industrial Corp Ltd (Johnnic) said on Friday an allocation of shares in its hugely oversubscribed black empowerment share scheme had been postponed by 10 days in order to collect application forms from far-flung areas.

Hazel Ralefeta, chairman of Johnnic's Ikageng Trust overseeing the share scheme, said more that 21,000 application forms had already been processed and expected that all forms would have been handled within the next 10 days.
"Due to overwhelming interest in the Ikageng share scheme, the allocation of the shares has been delayed," she said in a statement.
Ralefeta added that all participants who by Friday, June 27, had not received their full allocation will begin to earn interest on money they had deposited towards applying for the shares.
"Applications forms from remote areas in the country have taken longer than expected to arrive in Johannesburg for processing," she said.
Johnnic said earlier this month the special share offer of 9.1 million shares to historically disadvantaged members of the population had been 6.8 times over-subscribed.

The Ikageng scheme sets aside 6.4 million Johnnic shares, or six percent of the conglomerate, to smaller members of the black National Empowerment Consortium which bought a controlling 35 percent in Johnnic from Anglo American Corp of South Africa Ltd last year.
A further 2.7 million shares have been offered to individual blacks, Asians and people of mixed race only.
